windows.text: Once I’m attached, “I’m taking a chance on her” starts turning into “she’s the right person” after we’ve been together for a while.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Based on what? Sometimes I actually learned something, and sometimes nothing changed except that now I’m attached, so the new certainty is just harder for me to question.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: If I have sex with somebody quickly, that’s a reason not to move in quickly too.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Moving in together right away is basically getting into a common-law marriage without discussing it.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: It’s too easy for me to assume the relationship is going well just because we’re already entangled. So I want us to keep seeing friends, have some kind of community around the relationship, and pick actual dates to ask how it’s going.

windows.label: Human
windows.text:
I can know I want her much faster than I can know whether I want to raise children with her, live in community with her, or build a life with her.
At some point one of you will ask, “Why am I special to you? Why are you with me and not somebody else?” If the answer is basically, “We had sex and got hitched?” I don’t know, that’s a damn shame.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: And then there’s the situationship, which is hard to define because that’s basically the point. Usually it’s a happenstance relationship based on sex.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: There’s less communication, and what communication exists is more superficial. Yet it is obviously some kind of relationship even while one or both people refuse to name it. You’re regularly having sex, going out together, spending time alone together, and doing things you wouldn’t do with a regular friend.

windows.text:
It feels like it’s filling a relationship void, but only accidentally and occasionally, maybe just enough to keep you from looking for anything deeper.
It can go either way.

windows.label: AI-Generated
windows.text: Often the man wants to keep it undefined while the woman wants commitment, partly because she’s the one risking pregnancy.

windows.label: AI-Generated
windows.text: Whoever keeps it undefined gets the fun without the responsibility, but refusing to name the relationship doesn’t make the responsibility disappear.

windows.label: AI-Generated
windows.text: They don’t escape the existential void that another superficial fix creates, either.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Doomscrolling entertains you too.

windows.label: Human

And “Why are you making this heavy?” can be a real question. They may actually mean: don’t you want the fun, and are you about to give it up? My answer would be: I’m trying to understand whether this is really fulfilling me or if it’s drainingly superficial.
I had something sort of like that with H., although ours was much deeper than what people normally mean by situationship. We were (and still are) BFFs, and spent nearly all our time together. She was falling in love with me, and I wasn’t falling in love with her. She felt more like a sister to me, partly because I’m not attracted to white women.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: Ours wasn’t superficial, just painfully uneven.

windows.label: Human
windows.text:
For me, the window of objectivity starts closing abruptly once it seems like sex will definitely be happening soon and I’m flowing with that timeline. I begin idealizing her more, and after sex I may suddenly feel unable to leave because maybe she’s pregnant, etc.
Maybe I’m not representative of the modern degen dating scene. If you’re quite numb and used to casual sex, perhaps the window closes later, or even never. But for me, this is the pattern, and it seems like it would be healthy in a healthy, natural, small society.
The attachment theory part comes from my own experience and from reading I’ve done. Sex turns on bonding chemistry—oxytocin, dopamine, vasopressin—that usually biases us toward attachment.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: People call oxytocin the “love hormone,” as if getting more attached should make you feel closer and safer, but you can get more attached and more freaked out at the same time.

windows.label: Human
windows.text:
My own list isn’t especially flattering: I’m impulsive, and I idealize too much, although I don’t demonize. I’m very open and not very private. I care more about honesty than the standard romantic ideal. I still love my exes. After being deeply in love, I have overly high expectations, so I’m hard to please with a basic relationship.
I’m also extremely unique and have deeply held convictions many people won’t agree with. I’m anti-vax, anti-money, anti-civilization, etc. And I’m not yet living the way I want to live (astrology predicts I will by 2030 😃).
A woman should know that before she starts fitting me into the life or fantasy she already planned.
Key was an inner-child therapist and Reiki healer. Both Key and Bee were extremely curious and open-minded, which I loved about them. They were open to spiritual experiences, very connected to childlike wonder, and were always seeing what they needed to work on. They both meditated a lot.
I saw all that and thought anyone with that much spiritual depth and curiosity must already be far along on the path.

windows.label: Human
windows.text: That was my mistake. Their meditations may have helped them a lot. I still had no idea how either woman would act when a relationship got ugly. If somebody starts with enough trauma, huge progress can still leave a lot unresolved.

windows.label: Human
windows.text:
My own blind spot is that I have trouble understanding where people are at mentally and emotionally. A partner may agree with everything I say and then tell me later, “Didn’t you understand I was FAWNING?”
No, I really didn’t. If you’re fawning, tell me when you can, because I can’t know what’s happening in your head just because it feels obvious to you.
